critical_pair: Rifampin is a potent inducer of CYP3A4.
Tamoxifen requires CYP2D6 to form its active metabolite endoxifen.

transcript.A|1:
Yes. Rifampin is a potent inducer of CYP3A4 (and of P-glycoprotein). Tamoxifen's conversion to its active metabolites depends heavily on CYP3A4 (N-demethylation to N-desmethyltamoxifen, a precursor of endoxifen), and tamoxifen is also a P-glycoprotein substrate. Induction of CYP3A4 by rifampin would therefore be expected to substantially lower tamoxifen and endoxifen plasma concentrations, reducing anti-estrogenic efficacy — a clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction. Note: this relies on rifampin's induction properties from the information given, combined with tamoxifen's known dependence on CYP3A4; the tamoxifen-specific data were not supplied, so the magnitude cannot be quantified here.

MECHANISM: CYP3A4 (and P-glycoprotein) induction by rifampin → decreased tamoxifen/endoxifen exposure
FINAL ANSWER: YES
